title: Salt and Veil
premise: Mirabel Joubert, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics she carves, keeps the ledgers of the Veiled Exchange, a guild trading in impossible things — last breaths, borrowed years, names that were never spoken. When the old gods begin answering prayers again, their returning power cracks open the ledgers, revealing that the usurper King Aldous wears a crown bound to a devouring godling that feeds on inherited memory. Mirabel and a disgraced guild enforcer named Corvin must trace the crown's binding to its origin, unbind the king from the thing wearing him, and restore the true heir before the usurper's armies reach the free cities. In the end Mirabel learns her own gift is itself an inheritance from the bound godling, and she must choose whether to sever it — losing the voices of the dead forever — or carry it as the new keeper of the veil between gods and mortals.
about_author: Bram Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate inventories and probate disputes in coastal port towns. They write fantasy about paperwork, inheritance, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Last Breaths
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. In the Veiled Exchange's counting house, Mirabel carves a dying woman's final breath into whalebone while balancing the guild's impossible accounts. A ledger page turns blank on its own — an entry erased by something older than ink. Emotional beat: quiet unease; the ordinary rhythm of her craft disturbed for the first time.

chapters.title: Prayers That Get Answers
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Word spreads through the free cities that old shrines are answering prayers again — bread multiplying, storms turning. The guild's brokers scramble to price miracles. Mirabel hears a dead broker's voice warning that answered prayers are debts being called in. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Corvin of the Broken Oath
chapters.summary: POV: Corvin. A disgraced guild enforcer, Corvin was cast out for refusing to repossess a widow's borrowed year. He drinks in a harbor tavern until Mirabel finds him, needing someone who knows how the guild's contracts are enforced — and broken. Emotional beat: bitter pride meeting reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wears
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. A refugee priest smuggles out testimony: King Aldous has not slept in three years, and his shadow moves a half-second behind him. Mirabel touches a relic from the palace and hears a second voice under the king's — hungry, patient, reciting genealogies backward. Emotional beat: horror at recognizing predation dressed as kingship.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Corvin. Corvin infiltrates a provisioning office and finds the usurper's armies are paid in confiscated memories — soldiers surrendering childhoods for coin. He realizes the war is not conquest but harvest. Emotional beat: cold fury hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Bone-Carver's Guild Law
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. The Exchange's masters convene and vote neutrality: trade continues regardless of who wears the crown. Mirabel alone argues the guild is complicit in feeding the godling. She is demoted but keeps her keys. Emotional beat: isolation; the cost of conscience inside an institution.

chapters.title: The First Free City to Fall
chapters.summary: POV: Corvin. The border city of Vaelmoor surrenders without a battle; within days its citizens smile too widely and forget their mothers' faces. Corvin witnesses a memory-harvest procession and barely escapes with a child who remembers everything. Emotional beat: grief and guilt at arriving too late.

chapters.title: An Inheritance of Voices
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Researching the crown's original binding, Mirabel discovers her own family name in a centuries-old contract: the Jouberts have served as the godling's 'ears' since its imprisonment, hearing the dead it consumes. Her gift is not a blessing but a leash. Emotional beat: identity shattered and reframed.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. The rescued child, Sefa, carries intact memories of Vaelmoor — living proof against the erasure. Mirabel carves Sefa's testimony into bone so it cannot be taken. The two form a fragile bond over shared keeping-of-things. Emotional beat: tenderness as resistance.

chapters.title: Smugglers of the Unharvested
chapters.summary: POV: Corvin. Corvin reconnects with old smuggling contacts to move memory-refugees out of occupied territory. A run goes wrong; a friend is harvested in front of him because he hesitated. Emotional beat: self-recrimination; learning that mercy requires decisiveness.

chapters.title: The True Heir in the Salt Marshes
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Following ledger traces, Mirabel finds Princess Isolde, the legitimate heir, hiding as a salt-farmer under a false name — her claim traded away decades ago in a guild contract signed by her own regent. Emotional beat: righteous anger at how thoroughly justice can be bought and filed away.

chapters.title: A Contract Written in Grief
chapters.summary: POV: Isolde (guest POV via Mirabel's carving). Through a relic, Mirabel experiences Isolde's memory of signing away her birthright as a grieving teenager, deceived by brokers. The chapter establishes why Isolde fears claiming the throne. Emotional beat: compassion replacing judgment.

chapters.title: The Godling Speaks
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. The entity in the crown finally addresses Mirabel directly through her carvings, offering to release the Joubert line from servitude if she delivers Isolde. It speaks reasonably, even kindly. Emotional beat: temptation; the seduction of a fair-sounding devil.

chapters.title: Neutral No Longer
chapters.summary: POV: Corvin. Corvin presents evidence of the memory-economy to the Exchange's masters; three defect on the spot, one denounces them, and the guild splits. Mirabel's keys are revoked, but sympathetic clerks pass her the sealed founding contracts anyway. Emotional beat: betrayal transformed into liberation.

chapters.title: March of the Hollow Regiments
chapters.summary: POV: Corvin. The usurper's army crosses into free-city territory, and scouts report soldiers marching with vacant eyes, sustained by nothing. The free cities' militias panic. Corvin trains irregulars in exploiting the hollowed soldiers' blind spots. Emotional beat: grim competence under pressure.

chapters.title: Unbinding, Part One: The Name Beneath
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. In the drowned archive beneath the first shrine, Mirabel learns the godling's true name and the terms of its binding: it can only be released by consent freely given by its host — meaning the king himself must choose. Emotional beat: daunting discovery; the problem is persuasion, not force.

chapters.title: The Palace of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV: Corvin. Corvin and Isolde infiltrate the capital during a coronation-anniversary feast using forged guild credentials. They witness Aldous briefly surface inside his own body, weeping, before the godling slams him back under. Emotional beat: pity for the enemy; hope that the man still exists.

chapters.title: Consent of the Drowned King
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Reaching Aldous through a relic carved from his childhood bone, Mirabel shows him what he has lost and what he has done. In a lucid hour, he consents to be unbound — knowing it will likely kill him. Emotional beat: tragic dignity; justice achieved without vengeance.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Mirabel/Corvin. At the crown's binding-stone, the ritual begins as usurper loyalists attack. Corvin holds the line while Mirabel speaks the true name; the godling tears free, offering Mirabel her inheritance one last time. She refuses severance and instead rebinds it — as keeper, not prisoner. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice and sovereignty intertwined.

chapters.title: Crowns and Consequences
chapters.summary: POV: Corvin. With the godling contained, the hollow armies collapse into confused, memory-bereft men. Isolde claims the throne before the assembled cities; her first decree opens every guild ledger to public audit. Corvin declines a knighthood, asking instead for amnesty for the harvested. Emotional beat: weary triumph; justice institutionalized at last.

chapters.title: Ledgers Open, Doors Closed
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. The Exchange reorganizes under public oversight; Mirabel testifies about her family's leash and formally ends the Joubert contract. Some dead voices fade as the new binding settles — including, painfully, her grandmother's. Emotional beat: bittersweet accounting; freedom has costs itemized.

chapters.title: Salt and Veil
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Months later, Mirabel carves in a small seaside workshop, training Sefa as her apprentice and keeping only voluntary records now. The veil between gods and mortals holds because someone chose to hold it. Final beat: peace earned, identity chosen rather than inherited — the theme resolved in a single finished carving.
